addressed_requirements: The reviewer asked for the hypotheses and the results to follow the same order, offering either reorganization or cross-referencing. The response chooses one of the reviewer's options: it reorders the hypotheses to match the results & discussion sections.
The response gives a brief reason for choosing this direction: it is 'the most logical reporting structure'.
The response goes further and reorders the measures to match the new hypothesis order, which also helps the reader follow the paper.
remaining_gaps: Minor, not required by the reviewer: the hypotheses are pre-registered, so the authors could state that only the order changed and not the wording or content. They could also note that the order now differs from the pre-registration document. The response does not mention either point.
The response describes the changes only in words. No revised manuscript was supplied, so it cannot be checked whether the alignment is consistent throughout the paper.

evidence_refs.exact_quote: Either section could be re-organized but it would help the reader if they were aligned or at least cross-referenced.
We have now reordered our hypotheses to match the ordering of the results & discussion sections, as we believe this to be the most logical reporting structure.
We have also altered the order in which we present the measures to more closely reflect the new ordering of the hypotheses.

answer.rationale: The reviewer's concern is narrow: the hypotheses and the results are presented in different orders. The reviewer explicitly allows either section to be reorganized. The authors directly adopt one of these options, give a short reason, and also realign the measures section. On the text of the response alone, this fully meets the request. The missing statement about pre-registration transparency is a good-practice addition, not something the reviewer asked for, so it does not lower the rating. The actual revisions have not been verified.
